product.name: Shelfie
product.tagline: Your price list, open to AI shoppers.
product.audience: Sellers with a paper menu and no website, such as home bakers
valueProps: A photo of a paper price list becomes a PayPal catalog and a live shop
Any AI assistant finds the shop's agent door from its web address and orders through it
Buyers pay with PayPal, straight into the seller's own PayPal account

timeline.title: Shelfie
timeline.subtitle: Hi there! Welcome to Shelfie.
timeline.screen: Greeting card: the Shelfie lockup and "Hi there! Welcome to Shelfie."

timeline.narration: Rosa's bakery has no website, just a paper menu. An AI assistant just ordered from it, and Rosa got paid with PayPal.
timeline.screen: Cold open: the paper menu, then Rosa's dashboard as a paid order from an AI assistant lands (toast, row in To prepare, Paid).

focus.label: Ordered by an AI assistant · Paid with PayPal

timeline.narration: AI assistants are starting to shop for people. But they can only buy from shops with a website store. In one US survey, nearly half of food and lodging businesses had no website. Shelfie is for sellers with a paper menu and no website. One photo, and AI shoppers can order and pay.
timeline.screen: The handwritten Marigold menu, zooming in slowly; the one statistic, sourced; then the positioning line as a statement card.

onScreen.text: 47% of US accommodation and food-service businesses with employees had no website.
onScreen.source: US Census Bureau, Annual Survey of Entrepreneurs (data year 2016)

onScreen.text: Shelfie is for sellers with a paper menu and no website.
onScreen.sub: One photo, and AI shoppers can order and pay.

timeline.narration: It works in three steps. Snap your price list. AI shoppers order. And Rosa gets paid on PayPal.
timeline.screen: Roadmap card: the Shelfie lockup and three numbered steps, each appearing as it is spoken.

timeline.narration: Step one. Rosa snaps her price list. Claude, an AI model, reads every item and price.
timeline.screen: Phone: the Marigold photo picked, Read my menu, Reading your menu (Claude is reading every line), Check your menu: 10 items, 4 need you.

focus.label: One photo of the paper menu

timeline.narration: It only asks about what it wasn't sure of, like two for seven dollars. Rosa adds her PayPal email, so the money goes to her. Then every item goes into PayPal's catalog. Her shop is live, with photos.
timeline.screen: Phone: the “2 for $7” question (Looks right), the PayPal email (drawn as dots), Publish, Your menu is in PayPal; then the live shop page with its photos.

focus.label: It only asks what it isn't sure of
Her PayPal email: the money goes to her
Every item added to PayPal's catalog

timeline.narration: Step two. Every shop gets an agent door: a special address that AI assistants use to read the menu and order. It's built on MCP, an open standard.
timeline.screen: Laptop: the dashboard's Share tab: Your agent door, Give it to any AI assistant to order from you, the door's address.

focus.label: The agent door: where AI assistants order

timeline.narration: Here's Claude Code, an AI assistant, given only the shop's web address. It finds the agent door by itself, orders two almond croissants, and gets back a PayPal link.
timeline.screen: Terminal (sped up): Claude Code in an empty folder with only the shop URL; it finds the <link rel=alternate> “Agent door (MCP)” in the page, calls list_products and create_order, and prints the PayPal link.

focus.label: Given only the shop's web address
Finds the agent door on the page
Order placed · PayPal link to pay

timeline.narration: Another shopper uses the assistant on the shop page. She has a nut allergy. It warns her that the almond croissants contain nuts. She confirms, and it places the order.
timeline.screen: Laptop: the shop page's Order with an assistant: the request with a nut allergy, the Activity panel, the contains-nuts warning, then the order with Approve on PayPal.

timeline.narration: Step three. The buyer approves on PayPal. The money goes straight into Rosa's own PayPal account.
timeline.screen: PayPal's own checkout page ($27.00, Complete Purchase), then Shelfie's receipt: Paid, paid to Marigold Bakehouse's own PayPal account (masked).

focus.label: Paid to Rosa's own PayPal account

timeline.narration: Her dashboard shows the order as paid. Claude reads the order from PayPal and writes her a brief. It flags the nut allergy, so she can check before she ships.
timeline.screen: Laptop: Rosa's dashboard, the paid order in To prepare with its AI brief; the order page: AI brief by Claude, the nut-allergy warning.

timeline.narration: And an AI can't change the prices.
timeline.screen: Terminal: create_order with a price of 0.01 is refused: prices are set by the shop.

timeline.narration: Shelfie is for sellers with a paper menu and no website. PayPal runs their catalog and checkout, and pays them directly. AI reads the menu, lets assistants order, and writes the brief. For Rosa, paper is now enough.
timeline.screen: Summary card: who it's for, what PayPal does, what AI does, each row appearing as it is spoken.
